name: La Roche-Posay Effaclar

lead:
Effaclar is a skincare line from the French brand La Roche-Posay made for oily and acne-prone skin. According to Grokipedia, it includes cleansers, spot treatments, serums, moisturisers and toners, with actives such as salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide and lipo-hydroxy acid.
The appearance payoff is clearer-looking skin, less shine and less visible blemishes and clogged pores. A 2023 study of one product, the Effaclar sebo-controlling clay mask, measured improvements in acne lesions and sebum.

paras: Products are layered into a routine: cleanse, apply a treatment such as a benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid product, then moisturise. Grokipedia notes some products are labelled for ages 13 and up.
Benzoyl peroxide and salicylic acid products can cause dryness and irritation, so product labels advise following directions. The study of the clay mask reported safety measures alongside efficacy.

lead: La Roche-Posay Effaclar is a dermatologist-recommended skincare line for oily and acne-prone skin, according to Grokipedia, an AI-generated source [1]. It covers cleansers, medicated treatments, moisturisers, serums and toners [1].

Named actives include salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide and lipo-hydroxy acid, aimed at existing acne, new blemishes, the look of pores and oil shine [1]. The brand was founded in 1975 by pharmacist Rene Levayer and uses thermal spring water from the town of La Roche-Posay [1].

A published study of the Effaclar sebo-controlling clay mask enrolled 75 adults with oily or combination skin who used the mask twice weekly for four weeks. It reported significant improvements in acne-related outcomes, sebum content, skin evenness and hydration measures, with no significant change in pore area or porphyrin area [2].
infobox: Salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide, lipo-hydroxy acid

paras: Grokipedia lists the Effaclar Medicated Acne Face Wash with salicylic acid and the Effaclar BPO Multi-Target Acne Treatment with 5.5% benzoyl peroxide among the products, describing them as clinically tested [1].

A 2023 study of the Effaclar sebo-controlling mask in 75 adults over four weeks measured acne lesions, irritation, sebum and hydration with instruments such as a Sebumeter and Corneometer. It reported significant improvements in acne-related outcomes, sebum content, skin evenness and stratum corneum water content [2].
